title: The profile checklist in your sidebar
description: What Complete your profile counts, where to find the fields it means, and why a brand-new account has two outstanding - or three on a padel account.
body:
A warning under your name in the sidebar counts the profile fields you have not filled in yet. A new football account starts with two. A padel account starts with three - see below.

Finish your profile

  1. Select your name at the top of the sidebar. The block opens to show Edit User Profile and a warning: Complete your profile (2).

  2. Select Edit User Profile. Scoryboard opens Profile settings and jumps you to the first outstanding field.
  3. Fill in the fields tinted yellow under Personal Details. On a new account that is your Date of birth, because the sign-up form never asked for it.

  4. Fill in your Bio. It counts separately, which is why the sidebar says two.

  5. Select Save Changes.

On a padel account the count is three

A padel account has a second bio, and the checklist counts it. A new one reads Complete your profile (3), not (2).

  • Personal Details still reads "1 highlighted field is still missing", and it is still Date of birth. The sign-up form does not ask for it on either sport.
  • My Bio reads "2 highlighted fields are still missing". Both boxes are tinted: Bio and Padel Bio.

Best hand is not on the list. The sign-up form makes a padel account fill it in, so it is already there. Fill in both bios and the warning clears the same way.

What you will see

The count drops as you fill fields in. Once nothing is missing, the warning disappears from the sidebar altogether.

Each section on Profile settings counts its own fields. Personal Details and My Bio each say how many of theirs are outstanding, and the sidebar adds them up.

If it does not work

  • There is no warning under your name. Nothing is missing. Your profile is complete.
  • Save Changes does nothing. A required field is empty. The yellow tint shows you which.
  • Your date of birth is refused. You must be at least ten years old to use Scoryboard.
